messages.content: The response should include at least 22 pronouns. how does trade impact on the pharaoh powers

message.content:
Trade played a central role in shaping the powers of the pharaoh in ancient Egypt. It gave him access to rare resources that he could not obtain within his own borders. When he established trade routes with Nubia, Punt, and Mesopotamia, it extended his influence far beyond the Nile Valley.

We can see that the wealth they brought through trade—such as gold, ivory, and incense—strengthened his position as the divine ruler. He used those goods to fund temple constructions, which reinforced his religious authority. The priests themselves depended on him for those offerings, so their loyalty was tied to his control of trade.

He also used the profits from trade to equip and maintain his military. That gave him the power to project force into neighboring regions and protect the caravans that carried their goods. In turn, those military victories opened new markets, creating a cycle that made him even more powerful.

The pharaoh's diplomatic power grew because of those trade relationships. He could negotiate with foreign kings from a position of strength, and they often had to comply with his terms. His control over trade essentially made him the gatekeeper between Egypt and the wider world, and that position amplified his authority both at home and abroad.
